records.reference: ELEVEN O'CLOCK HAD STRUCK IT WAS A FINE CLEAR NIGHT THEY WERE THE ONLY PERSONS ON THE ROAD AND THEY SAUNTERED LEISURELY ALONG TO AVOID PAYING THE PRICE OF FATIGUE FOR THE RECREATION PROVIDED FOR THE TOLEDANS IN THEIR VALLEY OR ON THE BANKS OF THEIR RIVER
records.text: Eleven o'clock had struck. It was a fine, clear night. There were the only persons on the road, and they sauntered leisurely along to avoid paying the price of fatigue for the recreation provided for the Toledans in the valley or on the banks of their river.

records.text: Eleven o'clock had struck. It was a fine clear night. They were the only persons on the road, and they sauntered leisurely along to avoid paying the price of fatigue for the recreation provided for the Toledans in the valley or on the banks of their river.

asr.boundary: Quality only: each model runs serially and reuses only its own identical sample ranges/settings. Empty ranges bypass inference. All ASR edge/cut requests disable further trimming, isolating the evaluated policy. No ASR latency comparison.

limitations: These speakers appeared in earlier ASR evaluation; this is not a sealed model-ranking holdout.
Three transforms share each source utterance. Gain is synthetic electrical attenuation; SNR is nominal before clipping.
The five synthetic negative controls are reused, not independent environmental noise.

The 224ms history retention is not a bound on added finish delay: continued weak posteriors may sustain the aggregated score. The 1.424s raw control only accounts for the fixed history span; compare observed delays too.
Source clip end is a content-boundary proxy, not a last-phoneme annotation. No physical microphone or scheduling test.

The native Swift causal score matches the fixed reference formula on every frame. Synthetic gain/noise, shared active hardware and clip-end proxies do not prove device endpoint quality. GUI/default routing remains unchanged.
